name: core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register
prose: Slice cut the head: core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register(cmd, res_key, sa_res_key, aptpl, all_tg_pt, spec_i_pt, register_type) (target_core_pr.c:2039-2239). Precondition: cmd and cmd->se_dev are valid; the arguments come from a PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT REGISTER or REGISTER_AND_IGNORE_EXISTING_KEY parameter list. Postcondition: returns TCM_LOGICAL_UNIT_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE if cmd->se_sess or cmd->se_lun is NULL. It then looks up the registration for the command's I_T nexus with core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg (which takes a reference). No registration found: TCM_RESERVATION_CONFLICT if res_key is nonzero; 0 with no change if sa_res_key is zero; otherwise, without spec_i_pt, it calls core_scsi3_alloc_registration (nonzero: TCM_INSUFFICIENT_REGISTRATION_RESOURCES) and with spec_i_pt it calls core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port (nonzero result returned); in both cases it then returns core_scsi3_update_and_write_aptpl(dev, aptpl). Registration found: TCM_RESERVATION_CONFLICT if register_type is REGISTER and res_key differs from the stored key; TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST if spec_i_pt is set; TCM_INVALID_CDB_FIELD if the stored registration has all_tg_pt set and the incoming all_tg_pt is not (this check comes before, and applies to, both the key-change and the unregister case). Then with sa_res_key nonzero it sets the stored key to sa_res_key and pr_res_generation to core_scsi3_pr_generation(dev). With sa_res_key zero it calls core_scsi3_check_implicit_release (negative result: TCM_RESERVATION_CONFLICT), then under registration_lock frees, if the registration has all_tg_pt, every other all_tg_pt registration whose pr_res_key equals the incoming res_key and whose initiator name matches, frees the calling nexus's registration (pr_reg is then NULL), and if the released holder status is nonzero and the old type was a registrants-only type allocates a RESERVATIONS RELEASED unit attention for the remaining registrations before dropping the lock. Both of these branches finish with core_scsi3_update_and_write_aptpl(dev, aptpl) as the result. On the error returns after the lookup the reference is dropped by core_scsi3_put_pr_reg at the exit label; on the unregister path the reference is dropped inside __core_scsi3_free_registration (dec_holders = 1), so pr_reg is NULL at the exit and not put again. registration_lock is held only around the unregister block (__core_scsi3_free_registration itself temporarily releases it) and is not held on return.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the ALL_TG_PT check at 2135-2141 precedes the sa_res_key split so it also rejects a key change; old prose said only 'released'; rest of the old prose verified

name: target_scsi3_emulate_pr_out
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is target_scsi3_emulate_pr_out(cmd) (target_core_pr.c:3583-3733); the name target_emulate_pro_out does not exist. Precondition: cmd is a PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT se_cmd whose se_dev is valid and whose CDB and data buffer can be read. Postcondition: it returns TCM_RESERVATION_CONFLICT if DRF_SPC2_RESERVATIONS is set in the device's dev_reservation_flags; TCM_LOGICAL_UNIT_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE if cmd->se_sess is NULL; TCM_PARAMETER_LIST_LENGTH_ERROR if data_length < 24; and TCM_LOGICAL_UNIT_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE if transport_kmap_data_sg returns NULL, in which case nothing is mapped. Otherwise it reads the service action, scope and type from the CDB and the keys and flag bits (spec_i_pt, all_tg_pt, aptpl; for REGISTER_AND_MOVE aptpl and unreg) from the parameter list, forces aptpl to 1 if dev_attrib.force_pr_aptpl is set, and unmaps the buffer. Then it returns TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST if spec_i_pt is set with a service action other than REGISTER, and TCM_PARAMETER_LIST_LENGTH_ERROR if spec_i_pt is clear, the service action is not REGISTER_AND_MOVE and data_length is not 24. If TRANSPORT_FLAG_PASSTHROUGH_PGR is set the result of target_try_pr_out_pt is used. Otherwise it dispatches to core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register (REGISTER, and REGISTER_AND_IGNORE_EXISTING_KEY with res_key 0), _reserve, _release, _clear, _preempt (PREEMPT and PREEMPT_AND_ABORT) or _register_and_move, and uses its result; an unknown service action returns TCM_INVALID_CDB_FIELD at once. When the handler result is 0 the command is completed with target_complete_cmd(cmd, SAM_STAT_GOOD) and 0 is returned; a nonzero result is returned without completing the command here.
note: slice cut head; real name target_scsi3_emulate_pr_out; old prose omitted the three early returns before the buffer is mapped (3602-3620) and described the unknown-action return as reaching the done label (it returns directly)

name: tcmu_handle_completion
prose: Slice cut the head: tcmu_handle_completion(cmd, entry, keep_buf) (target_core_user.c:1320-1409). Precondition: cmd is a tcmu_cmd of udev whose ring entry is entry; keep_buf says whether the entry has TCMU_UFLAG_KEEP_BUF; cmd->se_cmd is the command still to be completed, or NULL if cmd already expired. Postcondition: three cases first. (a) TCMU_CMD_BIT_EXPIRED set: WARN_ON_ONCE(se_cmd); se_cmd is not completed and its priv is not cleared; ret stays true. (b) TCMU_CMD_BIT_KEEP_BUF already set: an error is logged, TCMU_DEV_BIT_BROKEN is set on udev, ret = false; the queue entry is not touched and se_cmd is not completed. (c) Otherwise: list_del_init on cmd->queue_entry, tcmu_cmd_reset_dbi_cur, then: with TCMU_UFLAG_UNKNOWN_OP the entry's scsi_status is forced to SAM_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and sense copy and data gathering are skipped; otherwise read_len = se_cmd->data_length, lowered to entry->rsp.read_len (read_len_valid) for a DMA_FROM_DEVICE command with TCMU_UFLAG_READ_LEN and nonzero rsp.read_len; on SAM_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION the sense buffer is copied into se_cmd and, if read_len_valid is false, gathering is skipped, otherwise SCF_TREAT_READ_AS_NORMAL is set; BIDI commands gather the data area with bidi true and DMA_FROM_DEVICE commands without it. Then se_cmd->priv is set to NULL and the command is completed with target_complete_cmd_with_length (read_len_valid) or target_complete_cmd. All three cases then reach the exit: with keep_buf false cmd's data area and cmd itself are freed (so in case (b) too, even though ret is false); with keep_buf true cmd is kept, TCMU_CMD_BIT_EXPIRED is cleared and TCMU_CMD_BIT_KEEP_BUF is set. The function returns false only in case (b), otherwise true.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): in the KEEP_BUF-already-set case the code goes to out (line 1342) and frees cmd when keep_buf is false; old prose first said cmd is left queued and later said it is freed

name: nvm_authenticate_store
prose: Slice cut the head: nvm_authenticate_store(dev, attr, buf, count) (retimer.c:251-314). Precondition: dev is a retimer device; buf is the written text; count its length. Postcondition: it calls pm_runtime_get_sync(&rt->dev) first. If mutex_trylock(&rt->tb->lock) fails, ret = restart_syscall() and the function goes straight to the runtime-PM exit: tb_retimer_unset_inbound_sbtx is not called and the lock was not taken. Otherwise, with the lock held: rt->nvm NULL gives -EAGAIN; a kstrtoint(buf, 10, &val) failure gives its error (rt->auth_status is not cleared in either case); otherwise rt->auth_status is set to 0. If val is nonzero it calls tb_retimer_set_inbound_sbtx(rt->port) and then: for AUTHENTICATE_ONLY it returns the result of tb_retimer_nvm_authenticate(rt, true); for any other nonzero value, if the NVM image is not flushed, it needs rt->nvm->buf (else -EINVAL) and runs tb_retimer_nvm_validate_and_write, stopping there if that fails or the value is WRITE_ONLY; it then calls tb_retimer_nvm_authenticate(rt, false) only for WRITE_AND_AUTHENTICATE (other values do nothing after the write). A zero val does nothing more. At the unlock exit tb_retimer_unset_inbound_sbtx(rt->port) is called if ret is nonzero or val == WRITE_ONLY (when ret is nonzero val is not evaluated, so this includes the -EAGAIN and parse-error returns), then the mutex is unlocked. On each return after the runtime-PM get, pm_runtime_mark_last_busy and pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(&rt->dev) are then called. The function returns ret when nonzero (the restart_syscall value, -EAGAIN, the parse error, -EINVAL or the error of the validate/write or authenticate call) and count otherwise.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): auth_status is cleared only after kstrtoint succeeds (274), and the trylock failure goes to exit_rpm, skipping unset_inbound_sbtx (259-262, 303-306)

name: usb4_port_sb_write
prose: Slice cut the head: usb4_port_sb_write(port, target, index, reg, buf, size) (usb4.c:1412-1457). Precondition: port is valid; buf is NULL or readable for DIV_ROUND_UP(size, 4) 32-bit words (that many dwords are read, which can be up to three bytes more than size). Postcondition: dwords = DIV_ROUND_UP(size, 4). It returns -EINVAL if port->cap_usb4 is 0. If buf is non-NULL it writes the dwords to the port data register through usb4_port_write_data, which returns -EINVAL if dwords > USB4_DATA_DWORDS (16), i.e. size above 64 bytes, or the register access error; with a NULL buf no data is written and no size check is made. It then writes the sideband command word (register reg, length size, write direction, target, retimer index only when target is USB4_SB_TARGET_RETIMER, pending bit set) to PORT_CS_1, returning a register access error, then polls the pending bit for up to 500 ms (error from usb4_port_wait_for_bit, e.g. -ETIMEDOUT), reads PORT_CS_1 back (register access error possible) and returns -ENODEV if the not-ready bit is set, -EIO if the result-code bit is set, and 0 otherwise.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): cap_usb4 cannot be a precondition when the code returns -EINVAL for it, and buf must cover DIV_ROUND_UP(size,4) dwords (1415, 1423); R1 NULL-buf point is covered above

name: hvc_dcc_console_init
prose: Slice cut the head: hvc_dcc_console_init (hvc_dcc.c:264-275), an __init console initcall with no parameters. Postcondition: it first calls hvc_dcc_check(), which writes a newline to the DCC channel and polls the DCC status for up to HZ/10 jiffies (and on CONFIG_HVC_DCC_SERIALIZE_SMP kernels may return true early on a non-zero CPU once core 0 was confirmed); if that returns false the function returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it calls hvc_instantiate(0, 0, &hvc_dcc_get_put_ops) and returns -ENODEV if that result is negative, otherwise 0. No locks are taken and no references are held after return.
note: contract dropped: the function touches hardware and global console state, so an integer-only contract does not apply; slice cut head

name: hvc_iucv_alloc
prose: Slice cut the head: hvc_iucv_alloc(id, is_console) (hvc_iucv.c:1048-1111), an __init function. Precondition: id is an index into hvc_iucv_table (below the configured number of devices); is_console is recorded in the new instance. Postcondition: it allocates a zeroed hvc_iucv_private (kzalloc; failure returns -ENOMEM), a zeroed sndbuf page (failure frees priv and returns -ENOMEM), an hvc terminal with hvc_alloc(id, id, &hvc_iucv_ops, 256) (an error pointer: the page and priv are freed and PTR_ERR is returned), sets irq_requested, fills in the IUCV service name, allocates the device with iucv_alloc_device (NULL: -ENOMEM) and registers it with device_register. A device_register failure puts the device reference. For the iucv_alloc_device and device_register failures the hvc terminal is also removed with hvc_remove before the page and priv are freed. Only on success is hvc_iucv_table[id] set to priv and 0 returned; on every failure the table entry is left unchanged and the cleanup that applies to the stage reached is done.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the cleanup listed is stage-dependent, not 'on every failure path' all four steps (1054-1111); contract dropped (weak, and function touches global tables)

name: udbg_hvc_putc
prose: Precondition: hvterm_privs[0] is NULL or points to an initialised hvterm_priv. Postcondition: returns nothing. If hvterm_privs[0] is NULL it returns at once. If c is '\n' it first calls itself with '\r'. It then loops: for proto HV_PROTOCOL_RAW it copies c into a local 16-byte bounce buffer and calls hvterm_raw_put_chars(0, buf, 1); for HV_PROTOCOL_HVSI it calls hvterm_hvsi_put_chars(0, &c, 1); for any other proto neither is called and count stays -1. The loop repeats while the last count is 0 or -EAGAIN and ends on any other value, including positive counts and other negative errors, which are ignored; so a character can be dropped when the put function fails with another error, and the function keeps retrying for as long as the put function returns 0 or -EAGAIN. With an unknown proto the loop ends after the first pass without sending anything. No value is returned and no error is reported.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): an invalid proto leaves count -1 and exits at once; the old 'later iteration spins forever' case needs proto to change mid-loop and is not shown by the code (229-255)

name: xenboot_write_console
prose:
Slice cut the head: xenboot_write_console(console, string, len) (hvc_xen.c:697-723). Precondition: string points to len readable bytes and is NUL-terminated (strchr scans from string+off until a NUL, so a missing terminator lets it read past len). Postcondition: returns nothing. If dom0_write_console(0, string, len) returns a non-negative value it returns at once. Otherwise, if not a PV domain, xen_hvm_early_write(0, string, len) is called and it returns. For a PV domain it writes "(early) " with domU_write_console and returns if that is negative. It then loops while off < len and strchr(string+off, '
') finds a newline at pos: linelen = (pos - string) + off, which is the correct segment length only when off is 0 (for off > 0 it is too large by off); if off + linelen > len the loop stops, otherwise it writes linelen bytes from string+off, then "
", and sets off += linelen + 1. This includes the first iteration: a newline found beyond len also stops the loop. Afterwards, if off < len, the rest string+off (len-off bytes) is written raw. With no newline the whole string is written raw with no "
". The domU_write_console results inside the loop and the final write are ignored.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): strchr needs a NUL-terminated string and the first newline also goes through the off+linelen>len break (713-720); the miscomputed linelen for off>0 was already in the old prose

name: autoconfig_16550a
prose: Slice cut the head: autoconfig_16550a(up) (8250_port.c:910-1061), a static void function. Precondition: up is a valid uart_8250_port and the caller holds up->port.lock (lockdep_assert_held_once). Postcondition: it sets up->port.type = PORT_16550A and ORs UART_CAP_FIFO into up->capabilities before anything else, and then returns by one of these paths. (1) CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_16550A_VARIANTS disabled and UPF_FULL_PROBE not set: returns without touching any register. (2) LCR set to CONF_MODE_A and EFR reads 0: EFR is written 0xA8; if it now reads nonzero the type is PORT_16650 with UART_CAP_EFR|UART_CAP_SLEEP (LCR is left at CONF_MODE_A and FCR is not touched), else LCR is set to 0, FCR is written with FIFO enable plus 64-byte mode and read back through IIR, FCR is written 0 and LCR 0, and the type becomes PORT_16550A_FSL64 if the IIR 64-byte bits are set; in both cases EFR is then written 0 and the function returns. (3) LCR set to CONF_MODE_B and EFR reads 0 and !broken_efr(up): autoconfig_has_efr(up) decides type and capabilities and the function returns. (4) National Semiconductor check: LCR is set to 0 and the MCR value is read, bank 2 is read; if the LOOP bit comparison is as expected MCR is toggled and restored to the original value (whether or not the chip is detected); if detected, the divisor is read and, if ns16550a_goto_highspeed succeeds, rewritten shifted left by 3, LCR is set to 0, up->port.uartclk = 921600*16, type PORT_NS16550A, capabilities |= UART_NATSEMI, return. (5) TI16750 check: FCR is written with FIFO enable (with and without 64-byte mode) with LCR 0 and with DLAB set and read back through IIR, ending with FCR = UART_FCR_ENABLE_FIFO and LCR = 0; if the two readings match 16550A and 16750 the type is PORT_16750 with UART_CAP_AFE|UART_CAP_SLEEP and the function returns. (6) XScale check: IER is saved, written with UUE cleared and, if UUE reads back as 0, with UUE set; if it reads back as 1 the type is PORT_XSCALE with UART_CAP_UUE|UART_CAP_RTOIE and the function returns with IER left with UUE set (not restored). Otherwise IER is restored to its saved value. (7) If the type is still PORT_16550A and size_fifo(up) is 64 the type becomes PORT_U6_16550A with UART_CAP_AFE.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): FCR is untouched when EFR works (PORT_16650 branch, lines 931-934), and LCR stays at CONF_MODE_A there; old prose also said MCR is restored only on the NS detection path although it is toggled and restored whenever the first LOOP test passes

name: cpm_uart_int_rx
prose: Slice cut the head: cpm_uart_int_rx(port) (cpm_uart.c:228-350). Precondition: port is embedded in a struct uart_cpm_port whose RX buffer-descriptor ring is initialised, rx_cur points into it, and port->state->port is a valid tty_port. Postcondition: returns nothing. Starting at pinfo->rx_cur it processes descriptors until one has BD_SC_EMPTY set or an early return happens. With CONFIG_CONSOLE_POLL, at the top of each descriptor iteration and again after the sysrq check for each character, a set serial_polled is cleared and the function returns immediately (no recycle of the current descriptor, no rx_cur update, no flip push). If tty_buffer_request_room(tport, datlen) returns less than the descriptor's length, a warning is printed and the function returns the same way. For each character port->icount.rx is incremented. If the descriptor status has any of BD_SC_BR, BD_SC_FR, BD_SC_PR, BD_SC_OV, the matching brk, frame, parity and overrun counters are incremented, port->sysrq is cleared, the status is masked with port->read_status_mask, the flag is TTY_BREAK, else TTY_PARITY, else TTY_FRAME by the masked bits (TTY_NORMAL if none left), and if masked BD_SC_OV remains the character becomes 0 with TTY_OVERRUN and the rest of the descriptor's characters are skipped; the character is then inserted. Otherwise a character consumed by uart_handle_sysrq_char is not inserted and any other is inserted as TTY_NORMAL. A processed descriptor has BR/FR/PR/OV/ID cleared and BD_SC_EMPTY set, and the pointer moves to rx_bd_base after a descriptor with BD_SC_WRAP, else to the next one. On reaching an empty descriptor it stores that pointer in pinfo->rx_cur and calls tty_flip_buffer_push(tport). On an early return, descriptors fully processed earlier in the same call have already been recycled but pinfo->rx_cur is not advanced.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): serial_polled IS checked at the top of the descriptor loop (247-252) as well as in the character loop (284-289), exactly as the old prose said; added that earlier descriptors stay recycled on an early return

name: imx_uart_start_tx
prose: Slice cut the head: imx_uart_start_tx(port) (imx.c:675-762). Precondition: called with the port lock held for a valid uart_port of an imx_port. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, changing nothing, if there is no x_char pending and the xmit kfifo is empty. If RS485 is enabled and tx_state is OFF, it sets RTS active or inactive in UCR2 according to SER_RS485_RTS_ON_SEND, calls imx_uart_stop_rx_with_loopback_ctrl(port, false) unless SER_RS485_RX_DURING_TX or rs485_rx_during_tx_gpio applies, sets tx_state to WAIT_AFTER_RTS and, if delay_rts_before_send > 0, starts the trigger_start_tx hrtimer and returns. Then (RS485 enabled) if tx_state is WAIT_AFTER_SEND or WAIT_AFTER_RTS it calls hrtimer_try_to_cancel(trigger_stop_tx), sets UCR4_TCEN if DMA is not enabled, and sets tx_state to SEND; with RS485 enabled and tx_state already SEND nothing is changed; with RS485 disabled tx_state is set to SEND. Without DMA it then sets UCR1_TRDYEN and returns. With DMA enabled: if an x_char is pending it clears UCR1_TXDMAEN, sets UCR1_TRDYEN and returns; otherwise, if the kfifo is not empty and the port is not tx-stopped, it calls imx_uart_dma_tx, which returns at once if dma_is_txing is already set and otherwise clears UCR4_TCEN and either starts a TX DMA transfer or fails (mapping or descriptor error, logged) without starting one; with an empty fifo or a stopped port it does nothing more. The port lock is not released.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): imx_uart_dma_tx returns early when dma_is_txing is set, before clearing UCR4_TCEN (633-638)

name: jsm_check_queue_flow_control
prose: Slice cut the head: jsm_check_queue_flow_control(ch) (jsm_tty.c:747-829); the item was labelled as an unnamed body. Precondition: ch is a valid jsm_channel with ch_bd and ch_bd->bd_ops set; ch_r_head and ch_r_tail describe the receive ring. Postcondition: returns nothing. qleft = ch_r_tail - ch_r_head - 1, plus RQUEUEMASK + 1 if negative. If qleft < 256: when CRTSCTS is set in ch_c_cflag and CH_RECEIVER_OFF is not yet set it calls bd_ops->disable_receiver(ch) and sets CH_RECEIVER_OFF; when CRTSCTS is not set and IXOFF is set in ch_c_iflag and ch_stops_sent <= MAX_STOPS_SENT it calls bd_ops->send_stop_character(ch) and increments ch_stops_sent. Independently, if qleft > RQUEUESIZE/2: when CRTSCTS is set and CH_RECEIVER_OFF is set it calls bd_ops->enable_receiver(ch) and clears CH_RECEIVER_OFF; when CRTSCTS is not set, IXOFF is set and ch_stops_sent is nonzero it resets ch_stops_sent to 0 and calls bd_ops->send_start_character(ch). Otherwise nothing is done. The function takes no lock itself.
note: slice cut head; real function jsm_check_queue_flow_control; old drop reason (unnamed body) does not apply; condition for XOFF is IXOFF with CRTSCTS clear (else-if at 784)

name: qcom_geni_serial_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: qcom_geni_serial_probe(pdev) (qcom_geni_serial.c:1735-1852). Precondition: pdev is a platform device bound to a node with qcom_geni_device_data match data. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise a negative errno, by these returns in order: -EINVAL if there is no match data; PTR_ERR of get_port_from_line (invalid line); -ENODEV if the port's private_data is already set; the error of geni_serial_resource_init; -EINVAL if there is no IORESOURCE_MEM resource 0; -ENOMEM if the RX buffer (non-console) or the port name allocation fails (both devm); the negative value of platform_get_irq(pdev, 0); at this point it sets private_data and platform drvdata, so the claim is kept for the later failures: the error of devm_request_irq, of uart_get_rs485_mode and of uart_add_one_port. If a wakeup IRQ (platform_get_irq_optional(pdev, 1) > 0) exists it calls device_init_wakeup(true) and dev_pm_set_dedicated_wake_irq; if that fails it calls device_init_wakeup(false), ida_free(&port_ida, uport->line) and uart_remove_one_port and returns the error. The other failure returns do not undo uport->private_data or drvdata (devm resources are released by the core).
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): right that get_port_from_line's PTR_ERR return was omitted; wrong that a TX FIFO -ENOMEM exists (only the rx_buf and name allocations, 1791-1802); wrong that the ida slot is not freed (ida_free at 1845)

name: stm32_usart_serial_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: stm32_usart_serial_probe(pdev) (stm32-usart.c:1765-1865). Precondition: pdev is a platform device bound to a stm32-usart node. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if stm32_usart_of_get_port gives no port; -EINVAL if of_device_get_match_data gives no info; -EPROBE_DEFER if dma_request_chan for "rx" returns -EPROBE_DEFER (nothing acquired). A non-deferral error from either dma_request_chan sets that channel to NULL (interrupt mode). If the "tx" request returns -EPROBE_DEFER the rx channel (if any) is released and -EPROBE_DEFER is returned. stm32_usart_init_port failure: both channels are released and its error returned. With wakeup_src set it enables wakeup capability and calls dev_pm_set_wake_irq; if that fails, wakeup capability is disabled, stm32_usart_deinit_port is called, both channels are released and the error returned (dev_pm_clear_wake_irq is not called on this path). Then the optional DMA rx/tx setups are tried; a failure releases that channel and falls back to interrupt mode. It sets drvdata to &stm32port->port, takes pm_runtime_get_noresume, set_active and enable, and calls uart_add_one_port; on failure it runs pm_runtime_disable, set_suspended, put_noidle, removes the DMA tx/rx buffers if the channels are set, calls dev_pm_clear_wake_irq and disables wakeup capability if wakeup_src, deinitialises the port, releases both channels and returns the error. On success it calls pm_runtime_put_sync and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the dev_pm_set_wake_irq failure jumps to err_deinit_port which skips dev_pm_clear_wake_irq (1799-1804, 1850-1854)

name: sunsab_convert_to_sab
prose: Slice cut the head: sunsab_convert_to_sab(up, cflag, iflag, baud, quot) (sunsab.c:680-772); its comment says it is called with port->lock held and local interrupts disabled (sunsab_set_termios does so). Precondition: up is valid, baud is nonzero (10000000 / baud) and quot is nonzero (uartclk / (16 * quot)). Postcondition: returns nothing. It sets up->cached_dafo to the character-length bits for CSIZE (CS5-CS8, anything else CHL5), ORed with DAFO_STOP if CSTOPB, DAFO_PARE if PARENB, and DAFO_PAR_ODD if PARODD else DAFO_PAR_EVEN (even parity bits are set whenever PARODD is clear, even with PARENB clear). It sets cached_ebrg = n | (m << 6) from calc_ebrg(baud, &n, &m), tec_timeout = 10000000 / baud and cec_timeout = tec_timeout >> 2. read_status_mask is TCD|TIME|RFO|RPF|CDSC in the low byte and (CSC|ALLS|XPR) << 8, plus PERR|FERR with INPCK and (BRK << 8) with any of IGNBRK|BRKINT|PARMRK. ignore_status_mask is 0, plus PERR|FERR with IGNPAR, plus (BRK << 8) with IGNBRK, plus RFO with both IGNBRK and IGNPAR, plus RPF|TCD if CREAD is clear. It calls uart_update_timeout(&up->port, cflag, uartclk / (16 * quot)), sets MODE_RAC in cached_mode, sets SAB82532_REGS_PENDING in up->irqflags, and calls sunsab_tx_idle(up) if SAB82532_XPR is set in irqflags. The lock stays held.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the REGS_PENDING and XPR/tx_idle steps are at 768-771 of this function, as the old prose said; earlier claims (baud!=0, PAR_EVEN when PARODD clear) were already stated

name: zs_console_write
prose: Slice cut the head: zs_console_write(co, s, count) (zs.c:1126-1169). Precondition: co->index selects a probed zs port (chip = index / ZS_NUM_CHAN, side = index % ZS_NUM_CHAN); the caller does not hold the scc zlock; s points to count readable characters. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under zlock (irqsave) it saves the R1 and R5 shadows, clears TxINT_ENAB in R1 (shadow and register) if it was set and sets TxENAB in R5 (shadow and register) if it was clear, and releases the lock. It then calls uart_console_write(&zport->port, s, count, zs_console_putchar); that helper takes zlock per character, converts newlines as uart_console_write does, and writes a character only if zs_transmit_drain returns nonzero for it, so a character can be dropped when the transmitter does not drain in time. Afterwards under zlock again it calls zs_line_drain(zport, irq) with irq = !irqs_disabled_flags(flags), clears TxENAB in R5 only if it was clear at entry, and, only if TxINT_ENAB was set at entry, sets it again in R1 and calls zs_raw_transmit_chars if zport->tx_stopped is false. The lock is released with interrupts restored.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): zs_console_putchar writes the character only if zs_transmit_drain succeeds (1115-1119), so 'all count characters are written' was overstated

name: adsl_state_store
prose: Slice cut the head: adsl_state_store(dev, attr, buf, count) (cxacru.c:332-431). Precondition: buf is a NUL-terminated string; count is not used (the result uses len = strlen(buf)). Postcondition: returns -EACCES without CAP_NET_ADMIN; -EINVAL if sscanf("%7s") cannot read a word; -ENODEV if the driver data (instance) is NULL; -ERESTARTSYS if mutex_lock_interruptible(&instance->adsl_state_serialize) is interrupted. With that mutex held it runs the command: "stop" or "restart" sends CM_REQUEST_CHIP_ADSL_LINE_STOP (failure: ret = -EIO, success: ret = len and poll = CXPOLL_STOPPED); "restart" then sleeps 1.5 s; "start" or "restart" sends CM_REQUEST_CHIP_ADSL_LINE_START (failure: ret = -EIO, poll unchanged; success: ret = len, poll = CXPOLL_POLLING), so a LINE_STOP failure is masked by a LINE_START success, and a LINE_START failure after a successful LINE_STOP leaves poll = CXPOLL_STOPPED; "poll" gives ret = len, poll = CXPOLL_POLLING; any other word leaves ret 0, which becomes -EINVAL with poll = -1. Then under poll_state_serialize: with poll == CXPOLL_POLLING, a CXPOLL_STOPPED state becomes CXPOLL_POLLING (poll stays POLLING), CXPOLL_STOPPING becomes CXPOLL_POLLING with poll = -1, and CXPOLL_POLLING or CXPOLL_SHUTDOWN are unchanged with poll = -1; with poll == CXPOLL_STOPPED, a CXPOLL_POLLING state becomes CXPOLL_STOPPING. adsl_state_serialize is then released and, if poll is still CXPOLL_POLLING, cxacru_poll_status(&instance->poll_work.work) is called directly (not queued). The function returns ret (len, -EIO or -EINVAL). poll_state can therefore change even on a -EIO return (restart where the stop worked and the start failed).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): restart with STOP ok and START failing returns -EIO but poll==STOPPED already moved POLLING->STOPPING (365, 377-386, 417-422); also cxacru_poll_status is called directly (427-428), not scheduled as the old prose said

name: _hardware_dequeue
prose: Slice cut the head: _hardware_dequeue(hwep, hwreq) (udc.c:820-899). Precondition: hwep and hwreq are valid; hwreq->tds is an initialised list of td_nodes. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL with no side effects if hwreq->req.status is not -EALREADY. Otherwise it sets req.status to 0 and walks hwreq->tds with a local actual starting at req.length. If a TD is still active it sets req.status back to -EALREADY, calls reprime_dtd for it only when the controller revision is CI_REVISION_22 or CI_REVISION_24 or the endpoint is isochronous and the endpoint's OP_ENDPTSTAT bit is clear, and returns -EBUSY at once without unmapping, without adding to req.actual (the local actual is discarded) and without touching later TDs; TDs handled earlier in the same call have already been unlinked and become pending_td. For each inactive TD it subtracts the remaining byte count from actual and sets req.status to the TD's raw status bits, then: halted gives -EPIPE and stops the walk, a data-toggle error -EPROTO and stops, a transaction error -EILSEQ and stops (for an isochronous endpoint the status is set to 0 and the walk continues), and a non-isochronous TX TD with bytes remaining gives -EPROTO and stops. A TD that does not stop the walk frees any previous hwep->pending_td (free_pending_td), becomes hwep->pending_td and is removed from hwreq->tds; the TD that stops the walk is not unlinked. After the walk (also after a stop or an empty list) it unmaps the request, debounces the scatter-gather list if hwreq->sgt.sgl is set, adds actual to req.actual, and returns req.status if nonzero (which can be -EPIPE, -EPROTO, -EILSEQ or other raw status bits) else req.actual.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): TDs completed before the active one have already been moved to pending_td/unlinked when -EBUSY is returned (879-883, 837-846); old prose said the TD list is not changed

name: acm_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: acm_probe(intf, id) (cdc-acm.c:1200-1612). Precondition: intf is a USB interface being probed and id->driver_info holds the quirk flags. Postcondition: returns 0 after allocating a struct acm and its resources (control and read coherent buffers, write buffers, control, read and write URBs, work, locks), calling usb_set_intfdata(intf, acm), creating the bmCapabilities file (and the country sysfs files when a country descriptor exists, skipped on failure), claiming the data interface with usb_driver_claim_interface when the interfaces are not combined, optionally clearing halts, and registering the tty device with tty_port_register_device. Before allocation it returns -ENODEV for the IGNORE_DEVICE quirk, for a missing interface in the NO_UNION_NORMAL and NO_UNION_12 cases, when there is no union descriptor, no 3-endpoint single interface and no call-management data interface, when the control or data interface is missing, and when probing a non-control interface of a non-combined pair; -EINVAL for a NULL extra-descriptor buffer or a zero-length one with no endpoint extra descriptors (the code does have these two checks), for a combined interface without exactly 3 endpoints, when the data interface class is not CDC data and neither the switched-interface case nor VENDOR_CLASS_DATA_IFACE applies, and when the data interface has fewer than 2 endpoints or the control interface has none; the error of usb_find_common_endpoints for a collapsed interface; then -ENOMEM if the acm allocation fails. Later failures go through the unwind labels (remove sysfs files, free URBs, coherent and write buffers, drop the data interface claim, tty_port_put) and return rv, which is -ENOMEM unless set by usb_driver_claim_interface or tty_port_register_device (so a minor allocation, a coherent allocation or a device_create_file failure returns -ENOMEM). The function does not itself clear intf's driver data on those failures.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the code does return -EINVAL for a NULL buffer and for zero-length descriptors (1255-1272); old 'leaving no driver data bound to intf' is not done by this function and was removed

name: usblp_write
prose: Slice cut the head: usblp_write(file, buffer, count, ppos) (usblp.c:744-840). Precondition: file->private_data is a usblp; buffer is a user address readable for up to count bytes. Postcondition: it takes usblp->wmut with mutex_lock_interruptible (interrupted: no lock and return -EINTR) and calls usblp_wwait; a negative result from that first wait is returned as the errno (-EINTR, -ENODEV, -EAGAIN when O_NONBLOCK and the previous write is not complete, -ENOSPC for paper out) with wmut released and nothing counted. Then for each block of up to USBLP_BUF_SIZE bytes it allocates a write URB (failure: -ENOMEM), anchors it, copies from user (failure: -EFAULT, URB unanchored and freed), and submits it (failure: no_paper cleared, wcomplete set, -ENOMEM kept or -EIO, URB unanchored and freed), then waits with usblp_wwait: if that wait fails with -EAGAIN or -ENOSPC the block's length is added to the count (and -ENOSPC sets no_paper), and for any wait error the URB is left anchored for cleanup on close; if usblp->wstatus is negative the block ends with -EIO; otherwise the URB's wstatus is added to the count and the loop continues until count bytes are done. wmut is released on every return after it was taken. The return value is the number of bytes counted if nonzero, else the errno that stopped the loop (or 0 when count is 0).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): -EAGAIN/-ENOSPC from the FIRST wait (756-758) are returned as negative errno; only the wait after a submit (800-811) counts the block as written, as the old prose said

Postcondition: returns sysfs_emit(buf, "%02x\n", ep->desc->field): the selected 8-bit descriptor field as at least two lowercase hex digits and a newline, and the number of characters written (3 for an 8-bit value). If buf is NULL or not page-aligned, sysfs_emit warns and returns 0 (it does not return -EINVAL). No locks are taken.
note: old prose said -EINVAL for an invalid buf: sysfs_emit returns 0 (fs/sysfs/file.c:759-761)

name: usb_set_interface
prose: Slice cut the head: usb_set_interface(dev, interface, alternate) (message.c:1591-1728). Precondition: dev is a valid usb_device. Postcondition: returns -EHOSTUNREACH if the device state is USB_STATE_SUSPENDED; -EINVAL if no interface numbered interface exists or no altsetting numbered alternate exists; -ENODEV if the interface is unregistering. It then calls usb_disable_interface(dev, iface, false), takes hcd->bandwidth_mutex and calls usb_disable_lpm: on failure it unlocks and returns -ENOMEM (no bandwidth change, LPM not re-enabled). It then sets streams = 0 on the current altsetting's endpoints and calls usb_hcd_alloc_bandwidth for the new altsetting: on a negative result it re-enables LPM, unlocks and returns that error. It then sends SET_INTERFACE with usb_control_msg_send (or uses -EPIPE when USB_QUIRK_NO_SET_INTF is set). If the result is -EPIPE and the interface has exactly one altsetting the failure is ignored and the altsetting is installed with a manual clear-halt of its endpoints; any other nonzero result (including -EPIPE with several altsettings) reinstates the old bandwidth, re-enables LPM, unlocks and is returned. On success the mutex is unlocked, and if the altsetting differs the old endpoint devices and sysfs interface files are removed; usb_disable_interface(dev, iface, true) is called, cur_altsetting is set to the new one, LPM is re-enabled, the endpoints are cleared of halt if the manual case applies, usb_enable_interface(dev, iface, true) is called, the sysfs files and endpoint devices are recreated only if the interface device is registered, and 0 is returned.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): usb_disable_interface is called both before the mutex (1623) and after it is released (1687) so the claim 'after, not before' is half true; other R1/R2 claims wrong: single-altsetting EPIPE handling and the -ENOMEM / alloc-bandwidth failure paths were already described correctly; old prose wrongly said streams are cleared only on success and that sysfs removal is conditional on registration

name: usb_set_configuration
prose: Slice cut the head: usb_set_configuration(dev, configuration) (message.c:2060-2285). Precondition: dev is a valid USB device. Postcondition: if dev->authorized is 0 or configuration is -1 the configuration is treated as 0 (unconfigure); otherwise the matching bConfigurationValue is looked up in dev->config. It returns -EINVAL, with nothing changed, if configuration is nonzero and not found. The new interface array and the usb_interface structures are allocated first; an allocation failure returns -ENOMEM with nothing else changed and the partial allocations freed. usb_autoresume_device failure returns its error with the new interfaces freed and the device state unchanged. After that, if the device is not in USB_STATE_ADDRESS usb_disable_device(dev, 1) tears down the old configuration (unbinding its drivers, actconfig = NULL, state back to ADDRESS). Then with hcd->bandwidth_mutex held: if dev->actconfig is non-NULL and usb_disable_lpm fails it unlocks, frees the new interfaces and returns -ENOMEM without calling usb_autosuspend_device (the autoresume reference stays); if usb_hcd_alloc_bandwidth fails it re-enables LPM if actconfig, unlocks, calls usb_autosuspend_device, frees the new interfaces and returns the error. Otherwise it initialises the new interfaces and sends SET_CONFIGURATION. If that transfer fails and a configuration was being set, the bandwidth is released, the new interfaces are disabled and put, and the device is left unconfigured. actconfig is set (to NULL when unconfiguring or after a failed transfer) and the mutex is unlocked. With no configuration the state becomes USB_STATE_ADDRESS, usb_autosuspend_device is called and the result of the control transfer (0 or an error) is returned. With a configuration the state becomes USB_STATE_CONFIGURED, the configuration string is cached if needed, LPM and LTM are re-enabled, each interface whose OF node is not disabled is registered with device_add (a device_add failure is only logged and that interface is skipped) and its endpoint devices created, usb_autosuspend_device is called and 0 is returned.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the -ENOMEM allocation failures happen before usb_autoresume_device and usb_disable_device (2093-2112), so 'state/config unchanged, no autosuspend' is right for them; the later usb_hcd_alloc_bandwidth failure is a different path already described with autosuspend; added the authorized==0 case and ignored device_add failures

name: usb_hub_create_port_device
prose: Slice cut the head: usb_hub_create_port_device(hub, port1) (port.c:739-839). Precondition: hub is a valid usb_hub with hdev set and port1 is a valid 1-based port number with no port device yet. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM if the usb_port or its pm_qos request cannot be allocated (nothing registered). Otherwise it records the port in hub->ports[port1 - 1], sets its power bit and registers the port device with device_register; a failure there does put_device and returns the error. It then gets the sysfs "state" dirent (failure: -ENODEV and device_unregister), adds the no-poweroff pm_qos request and the connector component (failure of either: sysfs_put of the dirent, device_unregister and the error returned). On those failure paths the function does not clear hub->ports[port1 - 1] or the power bit. After success of those steps it links the peer, sets runtime PM active, takes a runtime-PM reference that hub_configure() later drops, enables runtime PM and async suspend. If the hub does not support per-port power switching it returns 0. Otherwise it tries dev_pm_qos_expose_flags; if that fails it logs and still returns 0 (the kernel keeps the no_poweroff request); if it succeeds it removes the kernel request and frees it when dev_pm_qos_remove_request returns non-negative, then returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): dev_pm_qos_expose_flags failure returns 0 (820-823); old wording made it sound like a negative return; also hub->ports[] is not cleared on failure

name: dwc2_hsotg_irq
prose: Slice cut the head: dwc2_hsotg_irq(irq, pw) (gadget.c:3708-3915). Precondition: pw is a valid, initialised struct dwc2_hsotg registered as the handler's data. Postcondition: it first calls dwc2_is_device_mode, which reads a register (GINTSTS); if the controller is not in device mode it returns IRQ_NONE without taking hsotg->lock. Otherwise it takes hsotg->lock and loops (up to 8 passes) reading GINTSTS and GINTMSK and servicing, for each unmasked pending bit: RESETDET (writes GINTSTS_RESETDET, exits partial power-down or clock gating when applicable, lx_state = DWC2_L0); USBRST or RESETDET (writes GINTSTS_USBRST, calls dwc2_hsotg_disconnect, clears the device address in DCFG, and calls dwc2_hsotg_core_init_disconnected(true) if GOTGCTL shows BSESVLD and the device had been connected); ENUMDONE (writes GINTSTS_ENUMDONE, dwc2_hsotg_irq_enumdone); OEPINT or IEPINT (dwc2_hsotg_epint for each pending endpoint in DAINT masked by DAINTMSK); NPTXFEMP and PTXFEMP (the interrupt is disabled in GINTMSK, not cleared, then dwc2_hsotg_irq_fifoempty); RXFLVL (dwc2_hsotg_handle_rx); ERLYSUSP (writes GINTSTS_ERLYSUSP); GOUTNAKEFF (masked in GINTMSK, not cleared, and each unmasked OUT endpoint is handled: enabled isochronous ones get SNAK and EPDIS, halted non-isochronous ones get EPDIS and STALL, with EPENA added if not set); GINNAKEFF (sets DCTL_CGNPINNAK and dumps state); INCOMPL_SOIN and INCOMPL_SOOUT (the incomplete-isochronous handlers). It goes round again while bits in IRQ_RETRY_MASK were set and the retry count (8) is not used up. After the loop it calls dwc2_gadget_wkup_alert_handler if params.service_interval is set, releases the lock and returns IRQ_HANDLED.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): dwc2_is_device_mode reads GINTSTS before IRQ_NONE (3715); old prose also said all handled GINTSTS bits are cleared, but only RESETDET, USBRST, ENUMDONE and ERLYSUSP are written here

name: dwc2_hsotg_write_fifo
prose: Slice cut the head: the real function is dwc2_hsotg_write_fifo(hsotg, hs_ep, hs_req) (gadget.c:503-658); the name dwc2_hsotg_write_to_fifo does not exist. It is for PIO transfers. Precondition: hs_ep and hs_req describe an IN endpoint request; hs_req->req.actual, hs_ep->size_loaded and hs_ep->last_load are consistent. Postcondition: to_write = size_loaded - (req.actual - last_load); if that is 0 it returns 0 having done nothing. For a periodic endpoint without dedicated FIFOs it returns -ENOSPC after enabling GINTSTS_PTXFEMP if hs_ep->fifo_load is nonzero or the computed free space is <= 0. For a dedicated-FIFO endpoint other than 0 the free space comes from DTXFSTS; in the remaining case it comes from GNPTXSTS, and if the non-periodic queue has no slot it returns -ENOSPC after enabling GINTSTS_NPTXFEMP. The free space is capped at 512 bytes for non-periodic endpoints, to_write is capped at maxpacket*mc and, when it is cut to the free space, rounded down to whole packets; when either cap applies and dedicated FIFOs are not used, the PTXFEMP or NPTXFEMP interrupt is enabled. If the resulting to_write is <= 0 it returns -ENOSPC. Otherwise it sets req.actual to buf_pos + to_write, adds to hs_ep->total_data (and to fifo_load for periodic endpoints), writes DIV_ROUND_UP(to_write, 4) words to the endpoint FIFO, and returns -ENOSPC if that word count is >= the free space (a byte count) and 0 otherwise. It takes no lock.
note: slice cut head; real function dwc2_hsotg_write_fifo; old prose merged the arm-the-interrupt cases and attributed arming to every -ENOSPC return

name: dwc2_hcd_init
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is dwc2_hcd_init(hsotg) (hcd.c:5102-5358); the name dwc2_hcd_probe does not exist. Precondition: hsotg is a valid DWC2 instance with params, irq and a platform device with an IORESOURCE_MEM resource 0. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV at once if usb_disabled(). It may clear params.host_dma and dma_desc_enable (no dma_mask) and alters the global dwc2_hc_driver ops/flags. Failures: with CONFIG_USB_DWC2_TRACK_MISSED_SOFS the frame-number arrays can fail (-ENOMEM, error1 path); usb_create_hcd failure (-ENOMEM, error1); a missing memory resource (-EINVAL, usb_put_hcd then error1); dwc2_core_init failure (its error, same cleanup); workqueue, a host channel descriptor or the status buffer failing to allocate (-ENOMEM; the latter two via dwc2_hcd_release then usb_put_hcd); usb_add_hcd failure (its error, after destroying the unaligned, hsisoc and generic descriptor caches, then dwc2_hcd_release and usb_put_hcd). Every failure path ends with a logged "FAILED, returning" message. Failure of the descriptor caches only disables descriptor DMA, and failure of the unaligned cache is only logged. On success it sets device wakeup enabled (device_wakeup_enable), dumps state, enables global interrupts and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; real name dwc2_hcd_init; old prose omitted the -ENODEV return and the usb_create_hcd failure

name: dwc2_hc_chhltd_intr_dma
prose: Slice cut the head: dwc2_hc_chhltd_intr_dma(hsotg, chan, chnum, qtd) (hcd_intr.c:1800-1965). Precondition: hsotg, chan and qtd are valid and chan->hcint holds the channel's interrupt snapshot. out_nak_enh is set when snpsid >= DWC2_CORE_REV_2_71a, the channel is high speed OUT, and the type is CONTROL or BULK. Postcondition: returns nothing. If chan->halt_status is DWC2_HC_XFER_URB_DEQUEUE, or is DWC2_HC_XFER_AHB_ERR with descriptor DMA disabled, it calls dwc2_hcd_complete_xfer_ddma when descriptor DMA is enabled (only possible for URB_DEQUEUE) or dwc2_release_channel with the halt status otherwise, and returns. Otherwise it reads HCINTMSK and chooses one handler, in this order: XFERCOMPL (dwc2_hc_xfercomp_intr, preceded by dwc2_hc_ack_intr for an ISOC OUT channel); STALL; XACTERR with descriptor DMA disabled (dwc2_hc_xacterr_intr, after setting qtd->error_count = 0 if out_nak_enh and NYET, NAK or ACK is also set); XCS_XACT with descriptor DMA enabled (dwc2_hc_xacterr_intr, with no error_count change); AHBERR with descriptor DMA enabled; BBLERR; FRMOVRUN; and, when out_nak_enh is not set, NYET (dwc2_hc_nyet_intr), NAK not masked in HCINTMSK (dwc2_hc_nak_intr), ACK not masked (dwc2_hc_ack_intr), and if none of those an INT or ISOC channel gets dwc2_halt_channel(DWC2_HC_XFER_PERIODIC_INCOMPLETE). If no case matches (unknown reason for a non-periodic channel, or out_nak_enh set), it logs and goes to the error step: qtd->error_count is incremented, dwc2_update_urb_state_abn(..., DWC2_HC_XFER_XACT_ERR) is called, error_count is set to 3 if urb->actual_length >= urb->length, then dwc2_hcd_save_data_toggle and dwc2_halt_channel(DWC2_HC_XFER_XACT_ERR).
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): error_count is cleared only in the XACTERR (not XCS_XACT) branch (1857-1869), which the old prose could be misread to cover; clarified. R1/R2 points (ddma completion, ack+xfercomp) were already in the prose

name: dwc2_driver_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: dwc2_driver_probe(dev) (platform.c:439-647); the name dwc2_probe does not exist. The function allocates the hsotg itself and enables the low-level hardware itself. Precondition: dev is a DWC2 platform device. Postcondition: it allocates hsotg with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM), sets the DMA mask, maps register resource 0, runs dwc2_lowlevel_hw_init, gets the optional vbus regulator (an error other than -ENODEV is returned), and runs dwc2_lowlevel_hw_enable; these failures return the error without any cleanup. After that, failures of dwc2_get_dr_mode, dwc2_check_core_version, dwc2_core_reset, dwc2_get_hwparams, platform_get_irq, devm_request_irq, dwc2_init_params and, if activate_stm_id_vb_detection is set, of the usb33d regulator get or enable go to the common exit, which calls dwc2_lowlevel_hw_disable if ll_hw_enabled, and return the error. dwc2_drd_init failure additionally disables the usb33d regulator when it was activated. dwc2_gadget_init failure (when dr_mode is not host) and dwc2_hcd_init failure (when not peripheral, after removing the gadget with dwc2_hsotg_remove if it was enabled) also call dwc2_drd_exit first. On success it sets drvdata, hibernated = 0, creates debugfs, disables the low-level hardware when dr_mode is USB_DR_MODE_PERIPHERAL, and in peripheral or dual-role builds with the gadget enabled registers the UDC with usb_add_gadget_udc; if that fails it removes the gadget (dwc2_hsotg_remove), exits debugfs, removes the HCD if hcd_enabled, and takes the drd/usb33d/hw-disable exits. It returns 0 on success.
note: slice cut head; real name dwc2_driver_probe; old precondition was wrong: hsotg is allocated and the hardware enabled inside this function (445, 483)
